yaml.title: Phenological Changes in Pollination Pals
yaml.author: Aubrey Monaco
yaml.subtitle: Synchrony Shifts in the Ruby-throated Hummingbird and Preferred Flowers

markdown.markdown: With warming temperatures due to anthropogenic climate change, migrating birds are tending to move back to their breeding grounds earlier each year [1]. Along with this, flowers that certain migrating birds, like Ruby-throated Hummingbirds (*Archilochus colubris*), feed on may be changing the time of their first bloom due to climate change [2]. ![[Ruby-throated Hummingbird [3]]{style="color:darkblue;"}](data/rth_1.jpg){fig-align="center" width="400"} I want to investigate how the Ruby-throated Hummingbird has been shifting its spring migration patterns, and how the appearances of two spring ephemeral species it prefers to feed on during this migration, Red Buckeye (*Aesculus pavia*) and Red Columbine (*Aquilegia canadensis*), has changed (or not changed) over the past 10* years [4]. *My maps and graphs are from 2014 to 2025 to account for any incomplete datasets from 2025 ![[Red Columbine [5]]{style="color:darkred;"}](data/cb_1.jpg){fig-align="center" width="200"} ![[Red Buckeye [6]]{style="color:darkred;"}](data/rb_1.jpg){fig-align="center" width="226"} I predict that Ruby-throated Hummingbirds are migrating back to their breeding grounds earlier each year, and that they are arriving at higher latitudes increasingly earlier than lower latitudes. Additionally, I suppose that the first sightings of these preferred flowers will be earlier at higher latitudes and later at lower latitudes compared to previous years. So, as Ruby-throated Hummingbirds migrate back earlier, these flowers may not be available at lower latitudes for them to feed on. # Materials and methods ## 1. Install Packages and Load Libraries ```{r, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE} #install.packages("leaflet") # Dynamic maps #install.packages("leaflet.providers") # Different Basemaps #install.packages("leaflet.extras") # Heatmaps #install.packages("rinat") # Downloads iNaturalist data #install.packages("rnpn") # Downloads US National Phenology Network Data #install.packages("plotly") # Interactive graphs library(doParallel) # Download data in a parallel loop library(foreach) # Download data in a loop library(plotly) library(leaflet) library(leaflet.providers) library(leaflet.extras) library(rinat) library(rnpn) library(knitr) # Making tables library(kableExtra) library(rvest) # Used to download data from Journey North library(dplyr) # Mutating and filtering data library(lubridate) # Parsing date data library(tidyr) # Cleaning data library(ggplot2)# Plotting trends ``` ## 2. Flowers: Load iNaturalist and US NPN Data. - foreach, doParallel, and rinat package iNaturalist data download: - taxon_name is set to each desired species, place_id is set to 1 for the United States, maxresults is set to 10000 to ensure all data is downloaded, and quality is set to "research" to ensure verified data ```{r message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, eval=FALSE} #| code-fold: TRUE #Registering cores for downloading data num_cores <- parallel::detectCores() - 1 registerDoParallel(num_cores) #Parallel data download for both species 2005-2019 nat_0519 <- foreach(s = c("Aesculus pavia", "Aquilegia canadensis"), .packages = c("dplyr", "rinat"), .errorhandling = "pass", .combine = bind_rows) %:% foreach(a = c(2005:2019), .packages = c("dplyr", "rinat"), .combine = bind_rows) %dopar% { print(paste("Downloading data for year:", a)) Sys.sleep(60) get_inat_obs(taxon_name = s, year = a, place_id = 1, maxresults = 10000, quality = "research") } #Sequential data download for both species 2020-2025 nat_2025 <- foreach(s = c("Aesculus pavia", "Aquilegia canadensis"), .packages = c("dplyr", "rinat"), .combine = rbind) %:% foreach(a = c(2020:2025), .packages = c("dplyr", "rinat"), .combine = rbind) %do% { print(paste("Downloading data for year:", a)) Sys.sleep(60) get_inat_obs(taxon_name = s, year = a, place_id = 1, maxresults = 10000, quality = "research") } ``` - Individual datasets combined and written csv is loaded into environment as "nat_flower" ```{r, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE} #fl_all <- rbind(nat_0519, nat_2025) #write.csv(fl_all, "data/fl_all.csv") nat_flower <- read.csv("data/fl_all.csv") nat_flower <- nat_flower %>% filter(common_name %in% c("red columbine", "Red Buckeye")) ``` - rnpn package for NPN data download (automatically saves as a csv): ```{r, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, eval=FALSE} # Species IDs are available through the NPN's website (Red Buckeye = 784, Red Columbine = 147) npn_download_individual_phenometrics( request_source='Aubrey Monaco', years=c(2005, 2006, 2007, 2008, 2009, 2010, 2011, 2012, 2013, 2014, 2015, 2016, 2017, 2018, 2019, 2020, 2021, 2022, 2023, 2024, 2025), species_id=c(784, 147), download_path="data/npn_flower.csv" ) ``` ```{r} npn_flower <- read.csv("data/npn_flower.csv") ``` ## 3. Flowers: Combine the iNaturalist and NPN Data ```{r} # iNaturalist and NPN data are joined and duplicate observations are removed all_flower <- nat_flower %>% full_join(npn_flower) all_flower <- all_flower[!duplicated(as.list(all_flower))] all_flower <- all_flower %>% distinct() ``` ## 4. Flowers: Standardize and Mutate Data ```{r, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE} # dplyr and lubridate used to standardize and add columns from dates all_flower <- all_flower %>% mutate(observed_on = parse_date_time(observed_on, orders = c("mdy", "ydm", "dmy"))) %>% # Standardizes date formats mutate(year = year(observed_on)) %>% # Pulls year from date mutate(year_day = yday(observed_on)) %>% # Puts date into day out of 365 mutate(month = month(observed_on)) # Pulls month from date ``` ## 5. Flowers: Calculate Means of Early Period (2005-2013) - Found the mean date of first flower sightings from 2005 to 2013 and from March to May (when these flowers' bloom times overlap) [7,8] - Separated sightings into 3 bands of latitude to account for difference in average flowering times in across their range (grouped latitudes had similar "year_day" averages) ```{r, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE} fl_early <- all_flower %>% filter(year %in% c(2005, 2006, 2007, 2008, 2009, 2010, 2011, 2012, 2013) & month %in% c(3, 4, 5)) fl_early_all <- fl_early %>% mutate(latbin=cut(latitude, breaks = c(30,36,42,48), labels = c("30-36", "36-42", "42-48"))) %>% group_by(latbin) %>% mutate(mean = mean(year_day, na.rm=TRUE)) fl_means <- fl_early_all %>% group_by(latbin) %>% summarise(mean) %>% rename("Latitude" = "latbin", "Flowering Day Mean" = "mean") selected_fl <- fl_means[c(1, 25, 39), ] kable(selected_fl, format = "pipe", caption = '2005-2013 Flowering Time Means') ``` ## 6. Flowers: Calculate Means and Difference From 2014-2025 to 2005-2013 - Added a column (mean0013) based on table of flowering means by latitude - Used 6 bands of latitude for more specific analysis - Created a "difference" column, showing the difference in days of arrival between the early and current average using mean - mean0013 - Bound all of these bands into one dataset for plotting ```{r, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE} fl_new <- all_flower %>% filter(year %in% c(2014, 2015, 2016, 2017, 2018, 2019, 2020, 2021, 2022, 2023, 2024, 2025) & month %in% c(3, 4, 5)) %>% mutate(mean0513 = case_when( latitude > 30 & latitude < 33 ~ 81.95652, latitude > 33 & latitude < 36 ~ 81.95652, latitude > 36 & latitude < 39 ~ 99.73333, latitude > 39 & latitude < 42 ~ 99.73333, latitude > 42 & latitude < 45 ~ 114.30769, latitude > 45 & latitude < 48 ~ 114.30769)) fl_new_all <- fl_new %>% mutate(latbin=cut(latitude, c(30,33,36,39,42,45,48))) %>% group_by(latbin) %>% mutate(mean = mean(year_day, na.rm=TRUE)) %>% mutate(difference = mean-mean0513) %>% drop_na(difference) fl_new_difference <- fl_new_all %>% mutate(latbin=cut(latitude, breaks = c(30,33,36,39,42,45,48), labels = c("30-33", "33-36", "36-39", "39-42","42-45", "45-48"))) %>% group_by(difference) %>% select(latbin, difference) %>% rename("Latitude" = "latbin", "Difference in Ruby-throat Arrival Dates" = "difference") fl_new_difference <- fl_new_difference[c(1, 895, 222, 1425, 2656, 4115), ] ``` ## 7. Repeat Process for Ruby-throated Hummingbirds - Used data from eBird and Journey North in addition to iNaturalist and the US NPN. My eBird datasets can be found on figshare here: - 1995-2021: - 2022-2025: Visit each link and click "download" Or: Download the Ruby-throated Hummingbird data from eBird by visiting: , filter by year (I did this in two separate actions \[1995-2021 and 2022-2025\] to ensure I could download all of the data), filter by location (United States), and download as a csv. - iNaturalist data download: ```{r, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, eval=FALSE} #| code-fold: TRUE #Parallel data download for Ruby-throats 2005-2019 rth_0519 <- foreach(e = c(2005:2019), .packages = c("dplyr", "rinat"), .combine = bind_rows) %dopar% { print(paste("Downloading data for year:", e)) Sys.sleep(45) get_inat_obs(taxon_name = "Archilochus colubris", year = e, place_id = 1, maxresults = 10000, quality = "research") } #Sequential data download for Ruby-throats 2020-2025 rth_2025 <- foreach(e = c(2020:2025), .packages = c("dplyr", "rinat"), .combine = bind_rows) %do% { print(paste("Downloading data for year:", e)) Sys.sleep(45) get_inat_obs(taxon_name = "Archilochus colubris", year = e, place_id = 1, maxresults = 10000, quality = "research") } ``` ```{r, eval=FALSE} #Combined all iNat data into one data set for Ruby-Throats rth_nat <- rbind(rth_0519, rth_2025) write.csv(rth_nat, "data/rth_nat.csv") ``` - NPN data download: ```{r, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE, eval=FALSE} #| code-fold: TRUE #Ruby-Throated Hummingbird = 352 (Species ID) npn_download_individual_phenometrics( request_source='Aubrey Monaco', years=c(2005, 2006, 2007, 2008, 2009, 2010,2011,2012,2013,2014,2015,2016,2017,2018,2019,2020,2021,2022,2023, 2024, 2025), species_id=c(352), download_path="data/npn_rth.csv") ``` ```{r} npn_rth <- read.csv("data/npn_rth.csv") ``` Journey all_rth[!duplicated(as.list(all_rth))] all_rth <- all_rth %>% distinct() ``` - Parsing and mutating data ```{r, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE} #| code-fold: TRUE all_rth <- all_rth %>% mutate(Date = c(2005, 2006, 2007, 2008, 2009, 2010, 2011, 2012, 2013)) rthearly30 <- rth_early %>% filter(Month %in% c(2,3) & latitude > 29 & latitude < 33) %>% mutate(mean = mean(year_day, na.rm = TRUE)) rthearly33 <- rth_early %>% filter(Month %in% c(3,4) & latitude > 33 & latitude < 36) %>% mutate(mean = mean(year_day, na.rm = TRUE)) rthearly36 <- rth_early %>% filter(Month %in% c(3,4) & latitude > 36 & latitude < 39) %>% mutate(mean = mean(year_day, na.rm = TRUE)) rthearly39 <- rth_early %>% filter(Month %in% c(4,5) & latitude > 39 & latitude < 42) %>% mutate(mean = mean(year_day, na.rm = TRUE)) rthearly42 <- rth_early %>% filter(Month %in% c(4,5) & latitude > 42 & latitude < 45) %>% mutate(mean = mean(year_day, na.rm = TRUE)) rth_early_all <- rbind(rthearly30, rthearly33, rthearly36, rthearly39, rthearly42) rth_means <- rth_early_all %>% mutate(latbin=cut(latitude, breaks = c(29,33,36,39,42,45), labels = c("30-33", "33-36", "36-39", "39-42","42-45"))) %>% group_by(mean) %>% select(latbin, mean) %>% rename("Latitude" = "latbin", "Ruby-throat Average Arrival Dates" = "mean") selected_rth <- rth_means[c(1, 3, 6, 9, 17), ] kable(selected_rth, format = "pipe", caption = '2005-2013 Ruby-throat Arrival Means') ``` - 2014-2025 Ruby-throat dataset: ```{r, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE} #| code-fold: TRUE #"mean0513" taken from table of early means rth_new <- all_rth %>% filter(Year %in% c(2014, 2015, 2016, 2017, 2018, 2019, 2020, 2021, 2022, 2023, 2024, 2025) & Month %in% c(2, 3, 4, 5)) %>% mutate(mean0513 = case_when(latitude > 30 & latitude < 33 ~ 77, latitude > 33 & latitude < 36 ~ 110.6667, latitude > 36 & latitude < 39 ~ 112.6667, latitude > 39 & latitude < 42 ~ 137.125, latitude > 42 & latitude < 45 ~ 141 )) rth_30 <- rth_new %>% filter(Month %in% c(2,3) & latitude > 30 & latitude < 33) %>% mutate(mean = mean(year_day, na.rm = TRUE)) %>% mutate(difference = mean - mean0513) rth_33 <- rth_new %>% filter(Month %in% c(3,4) & latitude > 33 & latitude < 36) %>% mutate(mean = mean(year_day, na.rm = TRUE)) %>% mutate(difference = mean - mean0513) rth_36 <- rth_new %>% filter(Month %in% c(3,4) & latitude > 36 & latitude < 39) %>% mutate(mean = mean(year_day, na.rm = TRUE)) %>% mutate(difference = mean - mean0513) rth_39 <- rth_new %>% filter(Month %in% c(4,5) & latitude > 39 & latitude < 42) %>% mutate(mean = mean(year_day, na.rm = TRUE)) %>% mutate(difference = mean - mean0513) rth_42 <- rth_new %>% filter(Month %in% c(4,5) & latitude > 42 & latitude < 45) %>% mutate(mean = mean(year_day, na.rm = TRUE)) %>% mutate(difference = mean - mean0513) rth_new_all <- rbind(rth_30, rth_33, rth_36, rth_39, rth_42) rth_new_difference <- rth_new_all %>% mutate(latbin=cut(latitude, breaks = c(30,33,36,39,42,45), labels = c("30-33", "33-36", rth_new_difference[c(1, 250, 400, 650, 1490), ] ``` ## 8. Create Color Palettes ```{r} #Mapping colors to "difference" columns cpal <- colorNumeric(palette = "viridis", domain = fl_new_all$difference, na.color = NA) rpal <- colorNumeric(palette = "viridis", domain = rth_new_all$difference, na.color = NA) ``` # Results ### Trends in Flower Blooms (2014 - 2025) ```{r} leaflet(fl_new_all) %>% addProviderTiles(providers$Esri.WorldStreetMap, group = "World Map") %>% addProviderTiles(providers$OpenTopoMap, group = "Topo Map") %>% addLayersControl( baseGroups = c("World Map","Topo Map"), options = layersControlOptions(collapsed = FALSE) ) %>% addSimpleGraticule(interval = 3) %>% addCircleMarkers(~longitude, ~ latitude, radius = 5, stroke = FALSE, color = ~cpal(difference), label = ~scientific_name) %>% addLegend(pal = cpal, values = ~difference, title = "Difference From Early Average (days)", position = "bottomleft") %>% setView(-94.5786, 39.0997, zoom = 4) kable(fl_new_difference, format = "pipe", caption = '2014-2025 Difference in Flowering Times') ``` ### Trends in Ruby-Throated Hummingbird Sightings (2014 - 2025) ```{r} leaflet(rth_new_all) %>% addProviderTiles(providers$Esri.WorldStreetMap, group = "World Map") %>% addProviderTiles(providers$OpenTopoMap, group = "Topo Map") %>% addLayersControl( baseGroups = c("World Map","Topo Map"), options = layersControlOptions(collapsed = FALSE) ) %>% addSimpleGraticule(interval = 3) %>% addCircleMarkers(~longitude, ~ latitude, radius = 5, stroke = FALSE, color = ~rpal(difference), label = ~Age.Sex) %>% addLegend(pal = rpal, values = ~difference, title = "Difference From Early Average (days)", position = "bottomleft") %>% setView(-94.5786, 39.0997, zoom = 4) kable(rth_new_difference, format = "pipe", caption = '2014-2025 Difference in Ruby-throat Arrival Times') ``` ### Average Bloom/Arrival Times (2005-2013) ```{r} early_plot <- ggplot() + geom_point(data = fl_early_all, aes(x = mean, y = latitude, color = "Mean"), size = 0.1) + geom_smooth(data = fl_early_all, aes(x = mean, y = latitude, color = "Flowers"), method = "lm") + geom_point(data = rth_early_all, aes(x = mean, y = latitude, color = "Mean"), size = 0.1) + geom_smooth(data = rth_early_all, aes(x = mean, y = latitude, color = "Ruby-throats"), method = "lm") + labs(title = "Average Bloom/Arrival Times (2005-2013)", x = "Mean Arrival/Flower Date (Year Days)", y = "Latitude") + theme(plot.title = element_text(family = "serif", size = 12), axis.title = element_text(family = "serif", size = 10), panel.background = element_blank(), panel.grid = element_line(color = "lightblue"), legend.text = element_text(family = "serif", size = 10), axis.text = element_text(family = "serif", size = 10)) + scale_color_manual(name = "Legend", breaks = c("Mean", "Flowers", "Ruby-throats"), values = c("Mean" = "black", "Flowers" = "darkred", "Ruby-throats" = "darkblue")) ggplotly(early_plot) ``` Generally, Red Columbine and Red Buckeye flowering is spread over a large portion of Ruby-throat migration. ### Average Bloom/Arrival Times (2014-2025) ```{r} late_plot <- ggplot() + geom_point(data = fl_new_all, aes(x = mean, y = latitude, color = "Mean"), size = 0.1) + geom_smooth(data = fl_new_all, aes(x = mean, y = latitude, color = "Flowers"), method = "lm") + geom_point(data = rth_new_all, aes(x = mean, y = latitude, color ="Mean"), size = 0.1) + geom_smooth(data = rth_new_all, aes(x = mean, y = latitude, color = "Ruby-throats"), method = "lm") + labs(title = "Average Bloom/Arrival Times (2014-2025)", x = "Mean Arrival/Flower Date (Year c("Mean", "Flowers", "Ruby-throats"), values = c("Mean" = "black", "Flowers" = "darkred", "Ruby-throats" = "darkblue")) ggplotly(late_plot) ``` Generally, Red Columbine and Red Buckeye flowering happens over a shorter time within Ruby-throat spring migration. ### Observation Locations of Flowers ```{r} leaflet(all_flower)%>% addProviderTiles(provider = "Esri") %>% setView(-85.7664, 38.2469, zoom = 4) %>% addHeatmap() ``` ### Observation Locations of Ruby-throats ```{r} all_rth_map <- all_rth %>% filter(!is.na(latitude) & !is.na(longitude)) leaflet(all_rth_map)%>% addProviderTiles(provider = "Esri") %>% setView(-85.7664, 38.2469, zoom = 4) %>% addHeatmap(lng = ~longitude, lat = ~latitude) ``` # Conclusions Trends for Red Columbine and Red Buckeye show that the timing of first observations have changed from the 2005-2013 average. At the highest latitudes, flowering times are later than the early average. But for latitudes between 30 and 36, flowers have been sighted later than in previous years. Since these flowers are spring ephemerals, warmer winter temperatures, or more extreme heat in spring and summer, may cause this trend, as these flowers will not bloom under extreme heat, or until they have gone through a period of sufficient cooling [10]. Additionally, the average first observation date for Ruby-throated hummingbirds has been generally shifting earlier with increasing latitudes. These trends do somewhat align, especially at higher latitudes. So, these food sources will be available when Ruby-throats migrate back to higher latitudes earlier. But, Ruby-throats may may miss the flowering of these plants at lower latitudes. It is important to note that this dataset is relatively small, and data used to acquire average arrival/bloom dates for 2005 to 2013 was sparse. Additionally, since this data is collected from citizen science projects, the data may be more biased towards urban areas, and its distribution is not even. As shown in the heatmap for the flowers, observations do tend to be concentrated in urban areas. # References 1. Gill, J. A., Alves, J. A., Sutherland, W. J., Appleton, G. F., Potts, P. markdown.srcMarkdownNoYaml: # Introduction With warming temperatures due to anthropogenic climate change, migrating birds are tending to move back to their breeding grounds earlier each year [1]. Along with this, flowers that certain migrating birds, like Ruby-throated Hummingbirds (*Archilochus colubris*), feed on may be changing the time of their first bloom due to climate change [2]. ![[Ruby-throated Hummingbird [3]]{style="color:darkblue;"}](data/rth_1.jpg){fig-align="center" width="400"} I want to investigate how the Ruby-throated Hummingbird has been shifting its spring migration patterns, and how the appearances of two spring ephemeral species it prefers to feed on during this migration, Red Buckeye (*Aesculus pavia*) and Red Columbine (*Aquilegia canadensis*), has changed (or not changed) over the past 10* years [4]. *My maps and graphs are from 2014 to 2025 to account for any incomplete datasets from 2025 ![[Red Columbine [5]]{style="color:darkred;"}](data/cb_1.jpg){fig-align="center" width="200"} ![[Red Buckeye [6]]{style="color:darkred;"}](data/rb_1.jpg){fig-align="center" width="226"} I predict that Ruby-throated Hummingbirds are migrating back to their breeding grounds earlier each year, and that they are arriving at higher latitudes increasingly earlier than lower latitudes. Additionally, I suppose that the first sightings of these preferred flowers will be earlier at higher latitudes and later at lower latitudes compared to previous years. So, as Ruby-throated Hummingbirds migrate back earlier, these flowers may not be available at lower latitudes for them to feed on. # Materials and methods ## 1. Install Packages and Load Libraries ```{r, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE} #install.packages("leaflet") # Dynamic maps #install.packages("leaflet.providers") # Different Basemaps #install.packages("leaflet.extras") # Heatmaps #install.packages("rinat") # Downloads iNaturalist data #install.packages("rnpn") # Downloads US National Phenology Network Data #install.packages("plotly") # Interactive graphs library(doParallel) # Download data in a parallel loop library(foreach) # Download data in a loop library(plotly) library(leaflet) library(leaflet.providers) library(leaflet.extras) library(rinat) library(rnpn) library(knitr) # Making tables library(kableExtra) library(rvest) # Used to download data from Journey North library(dplyr) # Mutating and filtering data library(lubridate) # Parsing date data library(tidyr) # Cleaning data library(ggplot2)# Plotting trends ``` ## 2. Flowers: Load iNaturalist and US NPN Data. - foreach, doParallel, and rinat package iNaturalist data download: - taxon_name is set to each desired species, place_id is set to 1 for the United States, maxresults is set to 10000 to ensure all data is downloaded, and quality is set to "research" to ensure verified data ```{r message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, eval=FALSE} #| code-fold: TRUE #Registering cores for downloading data num_cores <- parallel::detectCores() - 1 registerDoParallel(num_cores) #Parallel data download for both species 2005-2019 nat_0519 <- foreach(s = c("Aesculus pavia", "Aquilegia canadensis"), .packages = c("dplyr", "rinat"), .errorhandling = "pass", .combine = bind_rows) %:% foreach(a = c(2005:2019), .packages = c("dplyr", "rinat"), .combine = bind_rows) %dopar% { print(paste("Downloading data for year:", a)) Sys.sleep(60) get_inat_obs(taxon_name = s, year = a, place_id = 1, maxresults = 10000, quality = "research") } #Sequential data download for both species 2020-2025 nat_2025 <- foreach(s = c("Aesculus pavia", "Aquilegia canadensis"), .packages = c("dplyr", "rinat"), .combine = rbind) %:% foreach(a = c(2020:2025), .packages = c("dplyr", "rinat"), .combine = rbind) %do% { print(paste("Downloading data for year:", a)) Sys.sleep(60) get_inat_obs(taxon_name = s, year = a, place_id = 1, maxresults = 10000, quality = "research") } ``` - Individual datasets combined and written csv is loaded into environment as "nat_flower" ```{r, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE} #fl_all <- rbind(nat_0519, nat_2025) #write.csv(fl_all, "data/fl_all.csv") nat_flower <- read.csv("data/fl_all.csv") nat_flower <- nat_flower %>% filter(common_name %in% c("red columbine", "Red Buckeye")) ``` - rnpn package for NPN data download (automatically saves as a csv): ```{r, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, eval=FALSE} # Species IDs are available through the NPN's website (Red Buckeye = 784, Red Columbine = 147) npn_download_individual_phenometrics( request_source='Aubrey Monaco', years=c(2005, 2006, 2007, 2008, 2009, 2010, 2011, 2012, 2013, 2014, 2015, 2016, 2017, 2018, 2019, 2020, 2021, 2022, 2023, 2024, 2025), species_id=c(784, 147), download_path="data/npn_flower.csv" ) ``` ```{r} npn_flower <- read.csv("data/npn_flower.csv") ``` ## 3. Flowers: Combine the iNaturalist and NPN Data ```{r} # iNaturalist and NPN data are joined and duplicate observations are removed all_flower <- nat_flower %>% full_join(npn_flower) all_flower <- all_flower[!duplicated(as.list(all_flower))] all_flower <- all_flower %>% distinct() ``` ## 4. Flowers: Standardize and Mutate Data ```{r, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE} # dplyr and lubridate used to standardize and add columns from dates all_flower <- all_flower %>% mutate(observed_on = parse_date_time(observed_on, orders = c("mdy", "ydm", "dmy"))) %>% # Standardizes date formats mutate(year = year(observed_on)) %>% # Pulls year from date mutate(year_day = yday(observed_on)) %>% # Puts date into day out of 365 mutate(month = month(observed_on)) # Pulls month from date ``` ## 5. Flowers: Calculate Means of Early Period (2005-2013) - Found the mean date of first flower sightings from 2005 to 2013 and from March to May (when these flowers' bloom times overlap) [7,8] - Separated sightings into 3 bands of latitude to account for difference in average flowering times in across their range (grouped latitudes had similar "year_day" averages) ```{r, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE} fl_early <- all_flower %>% filter(year %in% c(2005, 2006, 2007, 2008, 2009, 2010, 2011, 2012, 2013) & month %in% c(3, 4, 5)) fl_early_all <- fl_early %>% mutate(latbin=cut(latitude, breaks = c(30,36,42,48), labels = c("30-36", "36-42", "42-48"))) %>% group_by(latbin) %>% mutate(mean = mean(year_day, na.rm=TRUE)) fl_means <- fl_early_all %>% group_by(latbin) %>% summarise(mean) %>% rename("Latitude" = "latbin", "Flowering Day Mean" = "mean") selected_fl <- fl_means[c(1, 25, 39), ] kable(selected_fl, format = "pipe", caption = '2005-2013 Flowering Time Means') ``` ## 6. Flowers: Calculate Means and Difference From 2014-2025 to 2005-2013 - Added a column (mean0013) based on table of flowering means by latitude - Used 6 bands of latitude for more specific analysis - Created a "difference" column, showing the difference in days of arrival between the early and current average using mean - mean0013 - Bound all of these bands into one dataset for plotting ```{r, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE} fl_new <- all_flower %>% filter(year %in% c(2014, 2015, 2016, 2017, 2018, 2019, 2020, 2021, 2022, 2023, 2024, 2025) & month %in% c(3, 4, 5)) %>% mutate(mean0513 = case_when( latitude > 30 & latitude < 33 ~ 81.95652, latitude > 33 & latitude < 36 ~ 81.95652, latitude > 36 & latitude < 39 ~ 99.73333, latitude > 39 & latitude < 42 ~ 99.73333, latitude > 42 & latitude < 45 ~ 114.30769, latitude > 45 & latitude < 48 ~ 114.30769)) fl_new_all <- fl_new %>% mutate(latbin=cut(latitude, c(30,33,36,39,42,45,48))) %>% group_by(latbin) %>% mutate(mean = mean(year_day, na.rm=TRUE)) %>% mutate(difference = mean-mean0513) %>% drop_na(difference) fl_new_difference <- fl_new_all %>% mutate(latbin=cut(latitude, breaks = c(30,33,36,39,42,45,48), labels = c("30-33", "33-36", "36-39", "39-42","42-45", "45-48"))) %>% group_by(difference) %>% select(latbin, difference) %>% rename("Latitude" = "latbin", "Difference in Ruby-throat Arrival Dates" = "difference") fl_new_difference <- fl_new_difference[c(1, 895, 222, 1425, 2656, 4115), ] ``` ## 7. Repeat Process for Ruby-throated Hummingbirds - Used data from eBird and Journey North in addition to iNaturalist and the US NPN. My eBird datasets can be found on figshare here: - 1995-2021: - 2022-2025: Visit each link and click "download" Or: Download the Ruby-throated Hummingbird data from eBird by visiting: , filter by year (I did this in two separate actions \[1995-2021 and 2022-2025\] to ensure I could download all of the data), filter by location (United States), and download as a csv. - iNaturalist data download: ```{r, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, eval=FALSE} #| code-fold: TRUE #Parallel data download for Ruby-throats 2005-2019 rth_0519 <- foreach(e = c(2005:2019), .packages = c("dplyr", "rinat"), .combine = bind_rows) %dopar% { print(paste("Downloading data for year:", e)) Sys.sleep(45) get_inat_obs(taxon_name = "Archilochus colubris", year = e, place_id = 1, maxresults = 10000, quality = "research") } #Sequential data download for Ruby-throats 2020-2025 rth_2025 <- foreach(e = c(2020:2025), .packages = c("dplyr", "rinat"), .combine = bind_rows) %do% { print(paste("Downloading data for year:", e)) Sys.sleep(45) get_inat_obs(taxon_name = "Archilochus colubris", year = e, place_id = 1, maxresults = 10000, quality = "research") } ``` ```{r, eval=FALSE} #Combined all iNat data into one data set for Ruby-Throats rth_nat <- rbind(rth_0519, rth_2025) write.csv(rth_nat, "data/rth_nat.csv") ``` - NPN data download: ```{r, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE, eval=FALSE} #| code-fold: TRUE #Ruby-Throated happens over a shorter time within Ruby-throat spring migration. ### Observation Locations of Flowers ```{r} leaflet(all_flower)%>% addProviderTiles(provider = "Esri") %>% setView(-85.7664, 38.2469, zoom = 4) %>% addHeatmap() ``` ### Observation Locations of Ruby-throats ```{r} all_rth_map <- all_rth %>% filter(!is.na(latitude) & !is.na(longitude)) leaflet(all_rth_map)%>% addProviderTiles(provider = "Esri") %>% setView(-85.7664, 38.2469, zoom = 4) %>% addHeatmap(lng = ~longitude, lat = ~latitude) ``` # Conclusions Trends for Red Columbine and Red Buckeye show that the timing of first observations have changed from the 2005-2013 average. At the highest latitudes, flowering times are later than the early average. But for latitudes between 30 and 36, flowers have been sighted later than in previous years. Since these flowers are spring ephemerals, warmer winter temperatures, or more extreme heat in spring and summer, may cause this trend, as these flowers will not bloom under extreme heat, or until they have gone through a period of sufficient cooling [10]. Additionally, the average first observation date for Ruby-throated hummingbirds has been generally shifting earlier with increasing latitudes. These trends do somewhat align, especially at higher latitudes. So, these food sources will be available when Ruby-throats migrate back to higher latitudes earlier. But, Ruby-throats may may miss the flowering of these plants at lower latitudes. It is important to note that this dataset is relatively small, and data used to acquire average arrival/bloom dates for 2005 to 2013 was sparse. Additionally, since this data is collected from citizen science projects, the data may be more biased towards urban areas, and its distribution is not even. As shown in the heatmap for the flowers, observations do tend to be concentrated in urban areas. # References 1. Gill, J. A., Alves, J. A., Sutherland, W. J., Appleton, G. F., Potts, P.
